title: `resources/list`
description: Lists the resources a server exposes, each identified by a URI and described with a name, title, MIME type and optional size.
question: Can the agent discover the server's resources at all?
why: Resources are a server primitive alongside tools and prompts, and the one designed for application-controlled context rather than model-controlled action. A framework that exposes tools but not resources misses everything a server publishes as context.
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers publishing this. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.

notes.crewai: CrewAI 1.15.26: `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` exposes only `tools`. It has no resource or prompt API, so an agent built on it cannot reach this at all.
notes.genkit_js: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: `getActiveResources` turns each listed resource into a `dynamicResource` action named `<server>/<name>` with `description` and `uri`; `mimeType` (and `title`) are not kept.
notes.langchain: LangChain MCP Adapters 0.3.2: `load_mcp_resources` lists and reads in one step and returns LangChain `Blob` objects carrying the URI and MIME type. The resource's `name`, `title` and `description` are not carried, so the agent sees contents without the labels the server gave them.
notes.ms_agent_framework: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0: `MCPTool` has no resource or resource-template API; `resources/list`, `resources/read` and `resources/templates/list` are never sent. (`MCPSkillsSource` reads resources, but only `skill://index.json` and the skills it names.)
notes.semantic_kernel: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: `MCPPluginBase` loads tools and prompts only; it has no resource API.
notes.agno: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` lists and calls tools only; it has no resource or prompt API, so `resources/list` is unreachable.
notes.haystack: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPToolset` wraps tools as Haystack `Tool`s and has no resource or prompt API, and the `ClientSession` it opens is private to `MCPToolset._worker._client`, so there is no route to `resources/list`.
notes.smolagents: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): `smolagents.MCPClient` exposes only `get_tools()`, and the `ClientSession` lives on the private `MCPClient._adapter`. It has no resource or prompt API, so an agent built on it cannot reach this at all.
notes.dspy: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy's MCP support is `dspy.Tool.from_mcp_tool`, which converts one tool. It has no resource or prompt API, so resources and prompts stay on the caller's MCP session.
notes.beeai: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: `beeai_framework.tools.mcp` has `MCPTool` only. `MCPTool.from_client` lists and wraps tools, and BeeAI has no MCP resource or prompt API.
notes.crewai-native: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient` has `list_tools`, `call_tool`, `list_prompts` and `get_prompt` and no resource API, and `Agent(mcps=...)` turns only the tools into `BaseTool`s, so an agent built on it cannot reach this at all.
notes.google_adk_go: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): `mcptoolset.Toolset` exposes only `Tools()`, and the `*mcp.ClientSession` it opens stays inside its unexported `connectionRefresher`, so the caller has no session to call `ListResources` on.
